html:
SMTO-CTR-0022 — SMTO tried several times but couldn't write a plan

GUID: 40ebcdf9-7072-4549-8696-430e7073b387
Slug: task-contract-recovery-exhausted
Domain: CTR · Subsystem: task-contract

What happened

  • SMTO tried several times to write a plan for your request, and every attempt failed, so it stopped trying. SMTO didn't act on this request.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the Task contract step under the task and read Why this attempt was rejected for the last attempt. Every attempt failed, and the last reason tells you what actually needs fixing.
  2. If the reason says the plan was cut off, raise Task Contract maximum output tokens in Settings › Agent behavior › Task Contracts. Each attempt ran out of room, and more attempts with the same room fail the same way.
  3. If the reason is about the model or its service, ask the person who manages SMTO to check Settings › Setup › Model routing. A model that keeps failing or answering in the wrong form won't succeed on its own.
  4. After fixing the cause, send your request again as a new message, or select Retry on the task. Once the cause is fixed it's safe to try again; a new message uses your new settings, while Retry keeps the task's old ones.

What success looks like

  • The task shows Task contract generated and starts working.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with your request text, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't just raise Automatic retries or unrelated timeouts; more attempts won't help until the real cause is fixed.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Automatic Task Contract recovery reached its configured retry limit (transport started, no recorded stop reason) without producing an accepted contract.

What this means

  • Failure handling sees enabled automatic recovery with retry index at its configured ceiling, transport not explicitly unstarted and no recorded recovery-stop reason. This failure does not authorize execution for the rejected contract revision. Earlier revisions may already have effects; their original receipts remain authoritative. Diagnostic rendering makes no compiler or integrity-model call.

Why this can happen

  • Failure handling sees enabled automatic recovery with retry index at its configured ceiling, transport not explicitly unstarted and no recorded recovery-stop reason.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the saved final reason and attempt-specific retry counts instead of current global settings.

How to fix it

  • Read the final attempt's 'Why this attempt was rejected' in the Task contract activity (row 'Task contract automatic recovery exhausted') to find the actual compiler cause, such as truncation, an invalid submission or a provider failure, and correct it before an explicit Retry or a new task. Retry reuses the task's saved policy; changes to Automatic retries, Token increase per retry or Task Contract maximum output tokens under Settings > Agent behavior > Task Contracts apply only to new tasks, and raising normal execution output does not change compiler recovery.
  • Inspect the recorded final compiler cause. Correct that cause before requesting an explicit new attempt; increasing normal execution output does not change compiler recovery.

Relevant SMTO settings

  • Open Task Contract Output Allowance: task-contracts / task_contract_max_tokens. Applies to: new task.
  • Start a new task after changing this setting. Active and resumed tasks retain their captured values.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The actual final cause is resolved before any explicit new supported attempt.

What not to do

  • Do not change an unrelated timeout, budget or policy. Check whether the named setting applies only to a new task.

Technical notes

  • This failure does not authorize execution for the rejected contract revision. Earlier revisions may already have effects; their original receipts remain authoritative. Diagnostic rendering makes no compiler or integrity-model call.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
